education.mwEtymology: Latin educatus, past participle of educare (to lead out, educate), from e- + ducere (to lead)

parts.gloss: to be born; birth, race, nation
act, process, or result of; or noun suffix

nation.mwEtymology: Middle English nacioun, from Anglo-French naciun, from Latin nation-, natio (birth, race, nation), from nasci (to be born)

parts.gloss: to drive, cause to move, do
activity, act, legal process; noun suffix

action.mwEtymology: Middle English accioun, from Anglo-French accion, from Latin actiōn-, actiō (activity, act), from agere (to do, act) + -tiōn, -tiō (noun suffix)

parts.gloss: to stand, be in a particular place or state
place, condition, or act; noun suffix

station.mwEtymology: Latin statiōn-, statiō (act of standing), from stare (to stand) + -tiōn, -tiō

parts.gloss: act or process of; noun suffix

production.mwEtymology: Latin productiōn-, productiō (a bringing forth), from pro (forward) + ducere (to lead) + -tiō (noun suffix)

dictionary.mwEtymology: Medieval Latin dictiōnārium, from Latin dictiōn-, dictiō (speech, word, expression, from dicere to speak) + -ārium/-arius (relating to)

capacity.mwEtymology: Middle English capacite, from Middle French capacité, from Latin capacitat-, capacitas (state of being able to hold), from capax (able, spacious, from capere to take, hold) + -itas (noun suffix)
